patterns.name: Pinned LTS image
patterns.description: Use exact maintained Node LTS patch and Debian slim image, avoid latest/current tags.

alternatives: Node.js 22 LTS if a pinned dependency proves incompatible

patterns.name: Persist refreshed user tokens
patterns.description: Use RefreshingAuthProvider; its onRefresh event provides token data after refresh and should atomically persist it.

patterns.name: Send through Helix
patterns.description: Use the broadcaster user's Helix chat API and inspect successful result; current Twurple may throw ChatMessageDroppedError when Twitch drops a message.

patterns.name: Local EventSub WebSocket
patterns.description: Use EventSub WebSocket for a bot hosted on the end user's computer; do not add IRC or @twurple/chat.

patterns.name: Local HTTP server
patterns.description: Listen on 0.0.0.0 in the container and publish loopback-only on host by default.

patterns.name: JavaScript client generation
patterns.description: Pin prisma and @prisma/client to the same v6 release; use prisma-client-js while available because Prisma 7 prisma-client generates TypeScript.

conflicts: prisma-client is not compatible with this JavaScript-only source contract because it emits TypeScript

patterns.name: Prisma PostgreSQL adapter
patterns.description: Construct Prisma Client with PrismaPg and a runtime connection URL composed from the mounted secret without logging it.
patterns.codeExample: new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg({ connectionString }) });

patterns.name: Partial unique index
patterns.description: Enforce one active entry per queue/user in the database for waiting, called, and in_progress states.
patterns.codeExample: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON entries(queue_id, twitch_user_id) WHERE status IN ('waiting','called','in_progress');

dependencies.name: Docker Compose
dependencies.version: Compose v2; Node image node:24.20.0-bookworm-slim; PostgreSQL image postgres:18.6-bookworm

patterns.name: Ordered initialization
patterns.description: Compose can wait for DB health and one-shot migration success using dependency conditions.
patterns.codeExample: depends_on: { db: { condition: service_healthy }, migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully } }

conflicts: Compose local file secrets grant a file as a service secret; host-side bootstrap must set persistent file permissions compatible with mounted consumers

patterns.name: OAuth setup
patterns.description: Client Credentials POST to /oauth2/token validates the app pair; Authorization Code exchange provides the user token; validate user token on startup and hourly.

patterns.name: Reward management
patterns.description: Use app-owned custom rewards only. Manage scope is required for CRUD and redemption changes. The channel limit is 50 enabled plus disabled rewards; reward title max 45 and prompt max 200. Keep skip-request-queue false.

patterns.name: Redemption operations
patterns.description: GET pages of UNFULFILLED redemptions; PATCH status to CANCELED for points refund or FULFILLED for consumption; deletion of a reward with outstanding UNFULFILLED redemptions makes Twitch mark them FULFILLED.

patterns.name: Chat
patterns.description: Read chat with EventSub channel.chat.message (user:read:chat) and send through POST /helix/chat/messages (user:write:chat); verify response is_sent and honor 500-character limit.

patterns.name: Local bot transport
patterns.description: WebSocket transport is suitable for an end-user hosted chatbot; reward event subscriptions accept channel:manage:redemptions and chat reading needs user:read:chat.

unverifiedClaims.claim: A channel-specific 50-reward warning threshold of 45 and archive behavior do not change the Twitch fact that disabled/archived rewards occupy slots while they still exist.
unverifiedClaims.reason: The official API describes the 50 reward count including enabled and disabled; the product threshold of 45 is a user requirement.

unverifiedClaims.claim: Exact runtime behavior of every EventSub and Helix field through the installed Twurple release, including all reward/redemption enum normalization, must be contract-tested against actual SDK version.
unverifiedClaims.reason: Documentation and package metadata establish APIs, but exact serialized field mappings need implementation-time tests.

unverifiedClaims.claim: The local Compose file-secret mount and bootstrap permissions work on Windows Docker Desktop, macOS Docker Desktop, and Linux Docker Engine.
unverifiedClaims.reason: Compose file-backed secret details differ by platform, especially ownership/mode behavior.

recommendations.subject: JavaScript ESM across apps/*
recommendations.rationale: Matches the explicit no-TypeScript/no-transpiler requirement and preserves one runtime model.

recommendations.subject: PostgreSQL 18.6 and Prisma 6.19.3
recommendations.rationale: PostgreSQL 18.6 is currently maintained; Prisma 6.19.3 supports the required JavaScript client generator and prisma.config.mjs.

recommendations.subject: Twurple 8.2.0 packages at the same version
recommendations.rationale: npm metadata shows auth/api/eventsub-ws peer versions align at 8.2.0.

recommendations.subject: Prisma ORM 7 prisma-client generator
recommendations.rationale: Official v6 generator docs state prisma-client-js is deprecated as of Prisma 7 and Prisma 7 prisma-client emits TypeScript, violating the user constraint.

recommendations.subject: Unverified automatic retry for reward creation or point changes
recommendations.rationale: Network response loss does not prove whether Twitch applied the operation.

researchNotes: Research performed 2026-10-02 against official Twitch, Twurple, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Docker, Node.js documentation and npm package metadata. npm view reported @twurple/auth, @twurple/api and @twurple/eventsub-ws 8.2.0; Prisma CLI/client/adapter 6.19.3; Fastify 5.12.5; @fastify/static 10.1.5; Vitest 5.0.3; pg 8.23.1. Node.js v24 was LTS and PostgreSQL 18.6 was current supported minor on the checked release pages. No integration was called with a real Twitch credential. User authorization remains necessary for any eventual live Twitch test, but is not required for local unit/integration work.
